Message from The YMCAs of Québec 


Better anc better 


In 2009, The YMCAs of Québec held firm to its objectives as it continued to 
consolidate the organization and intensify its actions regarding communities in need. 
Given the uncertain socio-economic climate, we invested cautiously and relied 
on an even greater collaboration with our partners. This resulted in some great 
achievements of which we can be very proud. 


2009 was marked by the implementation of The YMCAs of Québec’s strategic plan, 
which will guide us for the next five years. The strategic plan, entitled “Reaching out. 
Giving more.”, gives meaning to our actions aimed at helping even more people 
across Québec. 


In terms of investments, in 2009 we continued with a very important project. The 
Cartierville Y centre, a grassroots initiative, is a model partnership between the 
community, the governments, and the YMCA, who came together to revitalize a 
neglected neighbourhood by providing the area with a community and fitness 
centre. We invite you to come discover this extraordinary building, which will quickly 
become the recreational and meeting place of choice for the people of Ahuntsic- 
Cartierville. 


In 2009, The YMCAs of Québec also implemented promising programs in many 
regions, including Quebec City. Notably, the Youth Eco Internship program now 
provides youth aged 15-30 with the opportunity to acquire work experience in an 
environment-related field within community organizations from coast to coast. As 
well, Alternative Suspension continues to move forward at full speed! This program, 
which was developed here to promote student success and which already serves 
more than 50 schools throughout Québec, has now been implemented in many other 
provinces. The program is so popular that it has even caught the attention of France, 
which wishes to implement our model as of this year. Our Y is spreading joy all around. 


As the YMCA approaches its 160" anniversary - a remarkable display of 
longevity that we will certainly highlight - we would like to thank the volunteers 
and employees who devote their time and energy to building a stronger world, 
a world where people stand united and lead more fulfilling lives, a world where 
everyone can grow, develop, and have their chance to shine. 


Dee Post Wopaus. Var tlaner.ul— 


Daniel Boisvert, Stéphane Vaillancourt, 
Chair of the Board of Directors President and Chief Executive Officer 


Message from The YMCAs of Québec Foundation 


The Leart PS ia sti eat ba Te 


We began 2009 with a certain degree of apprehension: was the recession going 
to shake everyone’s confidence and impact the Foundation’s activities? 
Fortunately, this did not occur. Our donors remained faithful to their 
philanthropic commitment and continued to believe in the positive social 
impact of The YMCAs of Québec. 


On our end, we ensured that their gifts were managed responsibly. For 2009, 
given the uncertainty of the markets and in line with many other foundations, 
we placed a moratorium on the distribution of income from our Endowment 
Fund. This allowed us to preserve the capital necessary to ensure the 
sustainability of the Y’s mission. The income distribution will resume in 2010. 


This did not impede us from continuing our development efforts. We were 
therefore able to practically complete phase | of the Kanawana Development 
Project, which will provide the camp with three-season eco-friendly facilities 
in order to welcome even more children from all walks of life. These achievements 
already make camp a model of community and sustainable development for 
the entire country. 


We also launched our “Destination Youth” fundraising campaign with the goal 
of creating an outdoor recreational area at the new Cartierville Y centre. This 
initiative has sparked the interest of the neighbourhood youth, who look 
forward to discovering the areas and activities developed just for them. 


Finally, our participation in the nationwide “YMCA Strong Kids” campaign was 
a huge success. Donors from Québec were very responsive and contributed 
over $300,000, which will be invested into homework help programs, day 
camps, hiring shadows for children with special needs, and other local 
community initiatives. 


All of this generosity warms our hearts. Thank you to our donors and 


volunteers, as well as all those involved, from near or far, in building a better 
world. 


Mize Ow 


Michael Goldbloom, Michael Novak, 
Chair of the Board of Directors President

BUILDING A 


NEW LIFE 
WITH THE Yr nnnes 


Her name is Graciela. His name is Miguel. Together they form 
a charming couple who live in Dollard-des-Ormeaux, a suburb of 
Montreal, with their three young children. Graciela and Miguel 
discovered the YMCA three years ago soon after they had 
arrived from Mexico, where they had lived up until that point. 


“By settling down here, our hope was to get a fresh start and, 
above all, to provide a better future for our children,” says Miguel. 
The couple did not know anyone here, and Graciela was 
pregnant with her third child. 


The welcome they received in Québec was wonderful. They 
immediately appreciated the kindness of the people, as well as 
the sense of freedom and safety that the city provided. The 
social worker with whom Graciela was in contact recom- 
mended the West Island Y centre and its childcare services. 
This was the start of a great adventure. 


“| started going to the Y and through the daycare | was able to 
meet other moms who shared the same concerns as | did. 
They were my first real contacts in this country,” states 
Graciela. During this time, Miguel learned about the Y’s fitness 
facilities. Wanting to get back into shape, he began to workout; 
first at the pool, and then in the exercise rooms. This is where 
he first developed his interest in massage therapy. 


The couple wasted no time in having their other family members 
discover the centre. Today, the entire family participates in the 
Y and benefits from the special family membership rate. Paolo, 
the eldest child at 8 years of age, enjoys the jungle gym and 
the aquatic facilities. Natalia, 4 years old, goes to the daycare 
5 days a week. As for little Luca, 2 years old, he participates 
in various Y activities adapted to his age. 


Aside from the recreational aspect and usefulness of its facili- 
ties, the YMCA has become an incredible community integra- 
tion tool for this wonderful Latin-American family. 


“We have no regrets about our decision to move to 
Québec, we feel a sense of fulfillment here. And 
the Y has truly become a second home for us,” 


The family membership is an 
economical package designed for 
two adults living in the same household 
and their children under 18 years of age. 
It includes all the benefits of the 


network membership, special discounts, 
and offers unlimited access to 
recreational activities adapted to 
each age group. 


says Graciela in closing. 


Nyhal (16 years old), 

Jonna (16 years old) and 

Karen (17 years old), participants 
in the Saint-Laurent Y centre’s 
Youth Zone and in the YMCA Youth 
Exchanges Canada program. 


Fort ait 


SEEING THE WORLD 
IN A DIFFERENT LIGHT 


The YMCAs of Québec 


It was cold on that day in Toronto, the kind of cold that leaves the city 
streets empty. But upon closer look, on the shores of Lake Ontario you 
could see a small group of brave youth who had come to gaze upon this 
inland sea that stretches out further than the eye can see. 


Nyhal, Jonna, and Karen, along with seven other boys and girls who par- 
ticipate in the Saint-Laurent Y centre’s Youth Zone, spent seven days in 
Toronto in the company of their guides Ruben and Mélanie as part of the 
YMCA Youth Exchanges Canada program. This program offers groups of 
youth aged 12-17 the opportunity to explore Canada in order to discover 
the diversity of its geography, cultures and communities, as well as to 
forge friendships with similar individuals in another community. 


These young Montrealers were pleased to renew acquaintances with 
their peers from Toronto who had come to visit them one month earlier. 
Their hosts had prepared an incredibly busy but rewarding schedule. The 
first cultural challenge they faced was the issue of language. For one 
week, they were immersed in the language of Shakespeare. 


After making the necessary tourist stops downtown, strolling through 
Chinatown (which Nyhal noted as being incredibly big!) and hanging 
around in the Arts District, the participants had their first taste of political 
life in Ontario by visiting City Hall and by attending parliamentary debates 
at the Legislative Assembly in Queens Park. 


Aside from visiting tourist spots, the group was able to really see the 
city from an insider’s perspective. This was thanks to the nature of the 
program, which is designed to promote interaction with “locals”. The 
hosts took their guests to visit their College, invited them to 
participate in community work and had them take part in 
a multicultural show. Together, they explored the city’s 
“everyday” neighbourhoods, interacting with the people 
who live and work there. 


“What was interesting was being able to discover 
different cultures and being able to constantly 
share ideas. Everyone was listening,” says Karen, 
who is also a member of the YMCA Youth 
Exchanges Canada advisory committee. 


“The participants saw the city from a different 
angle, one where the human aspect of things 
is valued,” explains group leader Ruben 
Escalante. It is said that trips can shape youth. 
If this is the case, then we can say that our 
exchanges open new horizons.” 


For these three youth exchange participants, the trip 
never really ended since they continue to be in contact 
with their friends from Toronto through Facebook. 


Eric, participant of the 
Downtown Y centre’s 
employment programs. 


Since 1985, the La Boussole - 
Employment Service has been providing 
free services to individuals with criminal 
records in order to help them reintegrate into 
the workforce or return to school.

of inmates and former inmates.

The HEART 
IS STRONG 


The YMCAs of Québec 


Eric had everything he needed to be happy: friends, a university 
education, and a good job. But at 38 years of age, he lost his job. 
What followed were feelings of discouragement and depression. 
Eric got hooked on drugs and started a long, downward spiral that 
eventually landed him behind bars. 


“In prison, | looked myself in the mirror and said, ‘This isn’t me. How 
could | have fallen so far?’” he recalls. 


The correctional services chaplain was the person who first helped 
him renew his belief in himself. “! decided to pull myself together 
and use all of the tools that were at my disposal. | wanted to 
become the Eric | once was.” Even though there were plenty of 
opportunities to do so in prison, Eric stopped using drugs. Instead, 
he headed to the office of the YMCA located within the correctional 
facilities, which offers various support services. One such service, 
designed to promote the social integration of inmates, is 
La Boussole - Employment Service. It is there that he began 
meeting Steve, the on-site counsellor, two days per month. Eric 
took an inventory of his skills, wrote his CV, and discussed what life 
after prison would be like. “Steve isn’t a therapist. But talking 
to him made me feel better and the obstacles seemed less 
insurmountable,” states Eric. 


Upon his release, Eric made use of a different facet of La Boussole’s 
services, only this time it was outside of the prison walls at the 
Downtown Y centre. Eric was pleasantly surprised by the warm 
welcome that awaited him at the Y, “There were times in my life 
when | believed people no longer had a heart. But | was wrong, the 
heart is strong.” 


La Boussole offered employment training to Eric along with a dozen 
or so other former inmates, integrated them into a job search group, 
and provided individual follow-up. 


As the months went by, Eric discovered that finding work was not 
easy when labelled an ex-con. The Y then pointed Eric in the 
direction of Les Démarcheurs, a program which lends support 
during the interview processes with employers. After many weeks 
of hard work and despite the obstacles, there was a light at the end 
of the tunnel. This spring, Eric found a job. 


This latest development has had an extremely positive impact on Eric’s life. 


His dreams can now become a reality.

Exciting projects in Quebec City 


Reach out to more people, offer more services. With the objective of one day 
building a new Y centre in Quebec City, The YMCAs of Québec launched, in 
collaboration with Quebec City, a study examining the different needs for fitness, 
recreational, and community activities in the borough of La Cité-Limoilou. Further 
studies will be required but a new Y centre, which would be the first one outside of 
the Greater Montreal area, will hopefully see the light of day in the neighbourhood 
of Saint-Roch! 


As part of growing our presence in Quebec City, The YMCAs of Québec inaugurated 
anew community presence in the borough of Duberger-Les Saules, which is situated 
in the neighbourhood of du Buisson, to meet the neigbourhood’s pressing needs. 
This disadvantaged sector of Quebec City is heavily populated and has little in the 
way of public infrastructures to offer services to the population. This new meeting 
place already welcomes about 60 youth participants in the Alternative Suspension 
program, along with many community groups that hold activities there on a regular 
basis. The Local YMCA-communautaire Les Saules was created thanks to the joint 
efforts of The YMCAs of Québec, the CSSS de la Vieille-Capitale, the borough of the 
Riviéres de la Ville de Québec, the county of Vanier, the Carrefour Jeunesse Emploi 
de la Capitale, and the Centre Ressources Jardin de Familles. 


Influenza A (H1N1) 


The threat of a much talked about influenza epidemic last fall resulted in a series of 
preventative strategies being implemented in the Y centres. A special committee 
was formed to coordinate communication between employees and volunteers, as 
well as with our clientele, and allowed the implementation of a variety of measures 
to ensure the continuation of our operations in case an epidemic situation arose. 
The Y’s plan addressed the issue from three angles: the protection of 
employees and members, the continuity of our operations, and the Y’s role in 
helping the community at large. 


Portage 2009: improve collaboration 


Last June, delegates from The YMCAs of Québec headed to Winnipeg to partici- 
pate in Portage 2009, a national conference bringing together all Canadian YMCA 
associations in order to develop improved collaboration across the country. Over 
400 volunteers and leaders from the YMCA renewed their commitment to support 
children and youth. The participants adopted strategies that focus on improving the 
health of the more than 735,000 children and youth currently served by the YMCA 
movement in Canada, and to enhance our outreach and impact with respect to 
families. 


For a greener Y 


The YMCAs of Québec is more than ever committed to sustainable development 
policies and practices. The organization adopted a vision and a strategic plan aimed 
at reducing its ecological footprint, developing ties with ethical and environmen- 
tally-conscious partners, and raising public awareness on these issues among its 
members, volunteers and staff. 


In 2009, a group of YMCA employees formed the Sustainable Y committee to turn 
these ideas into actions in each of the Y centres. The committee has already 
recruited an intern, has ensured the renewal of the /C/ on recycle certification, and 
has increased the Y’s focus on environmental awareness concerning its purchasing 
choices and the management of its facilities. The Y actively participated in the 
Semaine québécoise de réduction des déchets, World Water Day, Earth Day, 
campagne Défi climat, and in Environment week. 


The Management Resource Centre does its part! 


The YMCA Canada East Management Resource Centre (MRC) lends support and 
services to the 13 YMCAs and YMCA-YWCAs of the Maritimes. In 2009, the MRC 
East met with provincial groups in order to develop new areas of collaboration. As 
a result, YMCA leaders from across the country were dispatched to many YMCA 
centres in the Maritimes in order to help these YMCA management teams improve 
the organizational performance of their associations and centres. 


The most sought after expertise had to do with the development of facilities, 
fundraising, as well as training for employees and volunteers. The MRC East office 
located in Halifax managed two YMCA programs on the region’s behalf: Summer 
Work Student Exchange and Youth Eco Internships.

The 2009 Peace Medal recipients 


During the 2009 Peace Medal ceremony, The YMCAs of 
Québec honoured three exceptional individuals and 
two humanitarian organizations all of whom are dedicated 
to peace. Halah Al-Ubaidi, Noreen Majeed, Claudine- 
Michéle Desjardins, Leadership Services Youth and 
Sexualization Project, and Exeko distinguished them- 
selves through their actions that inspired peace at the 
local, national, and international levels. An honorary peace 
medal was also awarded to Senator and Lieutenant 
General Roméo Dallaire in recognition of his exemplary 
commitment to maintaining peace. The funds raised at 
this event benefitted the international youth exchange 
programs. Thanks to our sponsors: Power Corporation of 
Canada (Ambassador category); Centaure Financial 
Services Firm, and Solstice Financial Group (Youth for 
Peace category). 


Kanawana: significant progress 


Phase | of the Kanawana Development Project is coming 
to an end. The camp’s young campers and counsellors 
will soon be able to experience the 12 new three-season 
cabins erected this year on its wonderfully forested site in 
Saint-Sauveur. The cabins and the two sanitary facilities 
(completed in 2007), were made possible thanks to over 
$1.8 million in donations. The fundraising campaign is 
ongoing with the final objective being the construction of 
two learning pavillons in 2010-2011, thus completing 
Phase | of the development project. 


All these new facilities will allow the camp to offer envi- 
ronmental programming from spring to fall to a larger 
variety and greater number of clients including schools, 
families, and community groups. They will also help posi- 
tion the camp as a model of sustainable development 
for other outdoor centres and camps across the country. 
The aim of the Kanawana Development Project is to 
welcome even more children and youth from all walks 
of life and to give them a memorable experience through 
environmental education. Since 2004, the percentage of 
campers receiving financial assistance to attend camp 
has grown from 4% to 26%. 


Golf for a good cause! 


One hundred and forty golfers came out to the Pinegrove 
Country Club on a beautiful summer’s day in order to once 
again demonstrate their support for YMCA youth programs. 
Over $75,000 was raised to help fund the Y’s nine Youth 
Zones and the Association’s Youth Leadership programs. 
Thanks to all the volunteers who lent a hand to The 
YMCAs of Québec Foundation, and thanks to all our 
sponsors: Dectron internationale, Maison Ogilvy, Solmex 
Maintenance Inc. (Leadership category); CB Richard Ellis, 
SNC-Lavalin (Mentor category); Centaure Financial 
Services Firm, Morin Public Relations, Servicorp (Patron 
category).

Let’s adopt Adopt-a-School! 


Spearheaded by the Guy-Favreau Y centre, the Adopt-a- 
School program continues to do great things for elemen- 
tary school children in Montreal's Centre-Sud district. This 
year over $70,000 was invested in order to offer enriched 
educational programs, bursaries for students and financial 
assistance for campers. This was all thanks to our donors 
who chose to give to this noble cause. The Adopt-a-School 
program was created in 2006 thanks to a partnership 
between Desjardins Asset Management and The YMCAs 
of Québec with the aim of promoting equal opportunity. 
The program provides financial support to elementary 
schools located in disadvantaged neighbourhoods. Since 
2007, Desjardins Asset Management and its partners 
have adopted three schools in the Centre-Sud neigh- 
bourhood and have donated close to $400,000. 


Strong Kids campaign: goals met 


In 2009, The YMCAs of Québec participated in the nation- 
wide YMCA Strong Kids campaign which was a huge 
success. The campaign allowed the Y centres to raise over 
$300,000 which was redistributed, to such programs as 
homework help, day camps, seniors programs, and hiring 
shadows to help support children with special needs. With 
such a positive result The YMCA Strong Kids campaign is 
an experience worth repeating. 


New volunteer software 


A management data software called Volunteer 
Impact was launched in all of the centres by our 
volunteer managers. This new software provides, 
amongst other things, a clear understanding of 
volunteerism at the Y and will enable us to better 
communicate with the 1,450 volunteers of The 
YMCAs of Québec. This acquisition is part of the 
Human Resources team’s action plan. 


Heritage Club 


The 21° Heritage Club dinner, an event that highlights the 
Foundation’s Endowment Fund, was held in March 2009. 
Throughout the evening, Endowment Fund donors 
learned of the impact that their investments have had on 
youth. The evening culminated in the presentation of the 
Gabrielle and Maurice A. Massé Award to Judy and 
Michael Weil, a couple who has contributed greatly to 
the successes of The YMCAs of Québec through their 
involvement over many years as directors, employees, 
and volunteers.

Alternative Suspension grows 


The popularity of the Alternative Suspension program cannot be denied. This program, aimed at curbing 
student drop-out, is now implemented in nine cities across the province (Quebec City, Joliette, 
Valleyfield, Longueuil, Repentigny, Trois-Rivieres, Maskinongé, Huntingdon, Louiseville) and boasts a 
total of 16 points of service that serve over 60 high schools. Furthermore, seven Y centres in as many 
Canadian cities are interested in this program, developed by The YMCAs of Québec. They plan on 
implementing it in their communities in the coming year. The program has also drawn attention from 
the French government who may try out the program as of 2010. Alternative Suspension will receive 
financial support of $6.9 million over the course of five years from the National Crime Prevention 
Centre (NCPC), a division of Public Safety Canada. The Montreal team coordinates the national 
Alternative Suspension program. 


The YMCAs of Québec 


The YMCA Residence — busy as always 


While the number of asylum-seekers decreased in 2009 due to new federal policies, The YMCAs of 
Québec Residence continued to work with clients in need. New agreements have been established 
with the Office municipal d’habitation de Montréal in order to welcome homeless families for stays of 
up to two months. As well, agreements have been made with the ministére de /’Immigration et des 
Communautés culturelles in order to assist new refugees. 


The expansion of our catering service continued with the Y Residence preparing healthy meals 
during the course of the school year for 200 students attending Jean-Baptiste-Meilleur, Champlain, 
and Saint-Anselme schools. 


Black History Month at the Notre-Dame-de-Grace Y centre 


In order to highlight the historical contributions of the Black community, last February the 
Notre-Dame-de-Grace Y centre put on a show showcasing artists from the local community. 
The show featured gospel, tap dancing and R & B. Furthermore, with the help of its Youth Zone, the 
Y organized various events that included Caribbean cuisine and African music. 


A green alleyway 


In order to improve the quality of life of their neighbourhood, a dozen visually and hearing impaired 
youth collaborated with local citizens in helping make the Blanchard alleyway in Little Burgundy “green”. 
The initiative, supported by the Pointe-Saint-Charles Y centre’s Eco-quartier in Centre-Sud, consisted 
of planting a garden with perennials and shrubs. Students at the specialized McKay Center raised the 
funds needed for this project. 


The Westmount Y centre’s day camp 


There’s no stopping First Stop 


To celebrate the 10" anniversary of First Stop, in September the Downtown Y centre team and the 
First Stop workers increased its welcome and referral services to seven days a week rather than 
the usual six. In order to prevent homelessness, First Stop provides first-line services to vulnerable 
individuals with limited resources, who arrive in Montreal by bus and whose destination is unknown. 
First Stop helps over 800 people per year, offers referral services to some 75 organizations, and works 
in collaboration with more than 450 resources from the milieu. 


Rendez-vous Y 


Since January 2009 the young at heart have been meeting at the Downtown Y centre! Citizens aged 60 
and over benefit from the ability to use the Youth Zone while the youth are at school. They come to chat 
with their friends, make new acquaintances, share ideas, play board games, get back into shape and 
acquire new skills. 


Park facilitators 


How can the residents of a community improve their quality of life? One way is to have activities in 
public places. In the borough of Hochelaga-Maisonneuve, facilitators supervised by the neighbour- 
hood’s Y implemented family activities in two parks that had become areas to avoid. By having 
the local population reclaim these green spaces, youth gangs and those living a life of vagrancy and 
prostitution were driven away. This pilot project stems from the Plan d’action afin de contrer la 
violence et la consommation chez les jeunes established by the Concertation jeunesse Hochelaga- 
Maisonneuve.

Teens in training 


and YOUTH 


C-Vert 


In 2009, two additional Y centres participated 
in the C-Vert environmental youth program. After 
experiencing the outdoors first hand at camp 
Y Kanawana and having participated in workshops 
with environmental specialists, youth aged 14 to 
16 from the Notre-Dame-de-Grace, Saint-Laurent, 
and Hochelaga-Maisonneuve Y centres rolled up 
their sleeves and carried out green community 
development projects in their neighbourhoods. 
Notably, one of the projects involved the greening 
of an alleyway in Hochelaga-Maisonneuve. 


Youth Eco Internships 


Between now and the end of 2010, over 150 
unemployed Québec youth aged 15 to 30 will 
have had the opportunity to participate in a paid 
3 to 12 month internship in community organiza- 
tion across the province. These internships, which 
are administered by The YMCAs of Québec, focus 
on the environment and are offered as part of 
Canada’s Economic Action Plan. This is a unique 
opportunity for youth to gain experience in an 
up-and-coming field. 


After-School program 


The Notre-Dame-de-Grace, Hochelaga-Maison- 
neuve, and Pointe Saint-Charles Y centres wel- 
comed approximately 100 children from 
kindergarten to grade 6 as part of the After-School 
program. Weekdays from 3:30 p.m. to 6:00 p.m. 
and sometimes on Saturdays, the children 
received help with their homework and partici- 
pated in a variety of supervised activities including 
sports, arts, and more. Other activities, include 
science and cooking workshops, circus arts, 
improvisation, and choir.

Acelebrity rapper at the Y 


Popular French rapper Oxmo Puccino caused 
quite a commotion at the Y. The rapper, who has 
five albums to his credit, was in Montreal to 
perform at Metropolis as part of the Francofolies 
festival. He took advantage of his time in Québec 
by giving a workshop-conference to youth at the 
Du Pare Y centre. These youth participated in a 
variety of activities that led them to think critically 
about music and the challenges of the commu- 
nity. Much to their delight, Oxmo stayed and 
chatted with the youth for longer than his 
scheduled time. 


Healthy Kids Day: a wonderful event 


On May 30" and 31%, The YMCAs of Québec 
welcomed over 200 families in all of their Y centres 
as part of YMCA Healthy Kids Day. The event allowed 
children and parents to jointly take part in fitness 
and recreational activities, nutritional workshops, 
and more. The goal was to encourage healthy 
living and to strengthen family ties. 


Outdoor education for schools 


Over 500 students from six schools and 12 com- 
munity groups participated in outdoor education 
programs at camp Y Kanawana in 2009. The camp 
offered the groups outdoor education with 
content developed in partnership with the Com- 
mission Scolaire de Montréal (CSDM) and the 4-H 
Clubs of Québec. As part of the Ecole en forme 
et en santé, and the Bouger une heure par jour 
programs, the students received outdoor educa- 
tion with a pedagogical component that tied into 
the educational objectives of the classroom. 


Girlz Club: an emotional experience 


What are the living conditions of young girls 
around the world? What does the future have in 
store for them? In order to raise awareness on 
these issues for the Girlz Club members, the Notre- 
Dame-de-Grace Y centre organized a viewing 
of the movie “Des marelles et des petites filles” 
by director Marquise Lepage. The documentary, 
which illustrates what young girls in India, Peru, 
Yemen, Thailand, and Haiti are subjected to, 
stimulated a discussion and led to the implemen- 
tation of a child-sponsoring program in Haiti. 


Y Planet gets youth active 


The West Island Y centre inaugurated Y Planet; 
a new recreational area for youth aged 6 to 17. 
Y Planet includes interactive fitness games and 
videos that put their physical abilities, memory, 
and collaborative skills to the test. A YMCA pilot 
project, Y Planet originated from a desire to attract 
more youth to the Y centres, to offer them the 
opportunity to acquire healthy lifestyle habits, and 
to prevent obesity in children. The popularity of the 
project continues to grow. 


Car-free fun with the YMCA 
The YMCAs of Québec participated in the 7" edition of En ville sans ma voiture!, an 
j eco-friendly event held in September in downtown Montreal and simultaneously in 
many other cities in Canada and around the world. To mark the event, the YMCA 
dn offered a series of fitness activities to the general public in the outdoor car-free 
zone. The only participation requirement was getting to the event using only active

* ™ Seniors in Action 

The YMCAs of Québec The Du Parc Y centre has created a program to help seniors adopt healthy lifestyle 
habits and to integrate fitness activities into their everyday lives. Offered at 
the Du Parc Y centre and in certain low-cost housing projects and community 


centres in the neighbourhood, the program has been well-received by seniors as 
it allows participants to be supervised by a fitness specialist. 


Work out with your doctor 


Every Wednesday and Thursday evenings, The West Island Y centre welcomes 
the group Work out with your doctor, a fitness program which includes an educa- 
tional medical component. This activity was launched with the collaboration of the 
centre médical CardioGenix, the neighbourhood CLSC and CSSS, as well as the 
Lakeshore General Hospital. 


The Spring Challenge gets the crowds running 


The 6" edition of the Spring Challenge was an unprecedented success. Funds raised 
from the event helped support the Hochelaga-Maisonneuve Y centre’s commu- 
nity initiatives. Over 700 people came to run or walk through Maisonneuve Park 
and Montreal’s Botanical Garden over distances of 1, 2, 5, or 10 km. The Spring 
Challenge is an officially sanctioned race and is an event that is not to be missed. 
The funds raised help support youth leadership development, educational and 
fitness activities, and the integration of youth with special needs into the day camp. 


Following the trend! 


The times change and so do the trends. Many Y centres have added 
activities that are in high demand to their fitness programming, such 
as tap, zumba, and gymstick. Zumba, which is derived from rumba, 
is based on choreographed routines combining aerobic dance 
steps with movements that sculpt the body. Gymstick is a series 
of cardiovascular and muscular exercises using a stick with an 
elastic band. 


International Language School 


The International Language School of The YMCAs of Québec was well represented 
at various educational tradeshows, schools, and colleges in South America and 
Turkey. Our presence in Brazil resulted in a marked increase in registrations from 
that country. The International Language School also welcomed a group of 
students who wanted to perfect their English. While in Montreal, these students 
stayed at the Y Residence. 


Speaking of which, the Y Residence now offers housing for international students. 
They now have access to an entire wing of the building which includes rooms, a 
shared kitchen, a living room area, etc. 


An increase in registrations! 


The YMCA offers an array of training activities pertaining to Health, Fitness and 
Recreation, ranging from fitness instructor training to cardiopulmonary resuscita- 
tion classes, and from health workshops to lifesaving classes. The YMCA had a 
record year with almost 2,500 registrations in 2009! 


The YMCAs of Québec 


INTERNATIONAL INITIATIVES 


A $6.7 million agreement with CIDA 


Excellent news was received in January when YMCA Canada and the 
Canadian International Development Agency (CIDA) signed a $6.7 million 
five-year agreement to support the 43 YMCA centres in Canada for their 
initiatives in many African and Latin American countries. With this funding, 
the Downtown, Guy-Favreau, West Island, Saint-Laurent, and Westmount Y 
centres can now extend and strengthen their programs and partnerships with, 
amongst others, the YMCAs in Haiti, Honduras, Nicaragua, Ecuador, and 
Guatemala. 


As well, two YMCA employees participated in a special meeting of the Latin 
American and Caribbean Alliance of YMCAs (LACA) in order to help consoli- 
date their programs, gather resources, and find local sources of funding. 


YMCA/ACJ of Nicaragua 


The YMCAs of Québec collaborated with the YMCA/ACJ of Nicaragua in 
the implementation of a program promoting women’s rights in the hopes of 
reducing acts of violence against them. The project is based on the creation 
of a community network comprised of youth to help raise awareness and 
bring about change. This program has the financial support of the ministére 
des Relations internationales du Québec. 


Québec Social Forum 


Representatives from The YMCAs of Québec offered eight workshops as 
part of the Québec Social Forum held in Montreal in October. The event drew 
4,000 participants interested in the various issues and challenges society is 
faced with. 


No to sexist and violent toys 


Because we want children to live in a world without violence and sexism, 
The YMCAs of Québec led an awareness campaign inspired by the YMCA 
of Ecuador. The campaign promoted games and toys that are equally 
suitable for boys and girls and attempted 

to breakdown stereotypes and encourage 
cooperation. 


Intercambio for youth 


A delegation of eight youth aged 
15 to 17 accompanied two 
YMCA representatives from 
the Hochelaga-Maisonneuve and 
Westmount Y centres for a two- 
week trip to Nicaragua as part of 
the Intercambio exchange program. 
The experience of staying with a host 
family allowed them to meet their peers from 
the YMCA of Nicaragua and share ideas on common 
issues such as the environment, poverty, AIDS, 
and children’s rights. The youth also had the 
opportunity to understand the importance of 
Nicaragua’s community resources by visiting 
the new YMCA youth centre and by meeting 
some 20 dedicated volunteers. 


ae ns 


Youth from Québec in Nicaragué 


A workshop at the 
Québec Social Forum 


The Y at the World Social Forum 
in Brazil 

Sixty-two students from UQAM and the 
universities of Sherbrooke, Trois-Riviéres, 
and Ottawa, as well as their professors 
and a group of citizens, participated at the 
World Social Forum in Bélem, Brazil. The 
trip was organized by the International 
Initiatives department of The YMCAs of 
Québec. Before leaving, the participants 
were provided with training in order to 
become familiar with global social and 
economic realities, with a focus on Brazil. 
This served as an introduction to the way 
an international forum functions. Upon 
their return, they were asked to share their 
experiences. A gathering place for the 
alter-globalist movement, the social fo- 
rums are public places where notions of 
sharing, solidarity, and social justice are 
valued and debated. The group from the 
YMCA presented four workshops during 
the event. Next destination: Dakar in 
2011. 


Women first, then water 


Each of the Y centres of Québec played 
a part in hosting awareness activities for 
International Women’s Day (March 8) and 
for World Water Day (March 22). Over the 
course of these two days, volunteers and 
organizers gave meaning to the expres- 
sion “Think globally, act locally.” 


The YMCAs of Québec

Through its programs and activities, The YMCAs of Québec reaches 
nearly 100,000 people every year. This social audit would not be 


possible without the exceptional dedication of our 1,450 volunteers Ar statis atta 
and 1,300 employees.

Access for All policy: a Y for everyone 


For many years now, The YMCAs of Québec has implemented a flexible pricing system 
adapted to the income of its participants. Thanks to the Access for All policy, everyone can 
equally and fully benefit from the numerous programs and activities offered at their Y centre! 
In 2009, 5,293 individuals received a total of $ 775,861 in financial assistance from the YMCA. 


Innovation, Research and Development Fund 


The Innovation Fund supported five new community initiatives in 2009. The YMCAs allocated 
a total of $41,343 for the implementation of a day centre for seniors (Downtown), the 
C-Vert environmental program (Hochelaga-Maisonneuve), Seniors in Action (Du Parc), 
Moi aussi pour les enfants ayant des besoins spéciaux (Du Parc) and park facilitators 
(Hochelaga-Maisonneuve).
